exercises.prompt: Complete the past nominal clause governed by كَانَ: 'The house was large.'
exercises.explanation: كَانَ keeps its subject (البَيْتُ) nominative and places its predicate (khabar kāna) in the accusative: كَبِيرًا.

feedback.rule: Ism kāna is nominative (marfūʿ); khabar kāna is accusative (manṣūb).

exercises.prompt: Which suffix attaches to a verb to express 'me' (1st-person singular direct object, e.g., 'he taught me')?
exercises.explanation: Verbs take the protective nūn (nūn al-wiqāyah) before the 1st-person singular object pronoun: ـنِي.

feedback.rule: Nouns take ـِي ('my'); verbs take ـنِي ('me').
feedback.caseOrMood: In the place of accusative (فِي مَحَلِّ نَصْبٍ)

exercises.prompt: True or False: In كَانَ العِلْمُ نَافِعًا, the word العِلْمُ is accusative.
exercises.explanation: False. العِلْمُ is ism kāna and remains nominative (marfūʿ); only khabar kāna (نَافِعًا) becomes accusative.

feedback.rule: كَانَ leaves its subject nominative and turns its predicate accusative.
